claims.text: Small cell: platinum (cisplatin or carboplatin) plus a topoisomerase inhibitor, with or followed by immunotherapy;
claims.quote: Chemotherapy regimens of topoisomerase inhibitors and a platinum compound (either cisplatin or carboplatin) are commonly used in combination with or followed by immunotherapy.

claims.text: extensive stage: chemotherapy plus atezolizumab or durvalumab.
claims.quote: Systemic chemoimmunotherapy (eg, chemotherapy plus atezolizumab or durvalumab) is typically administered for patients with extensive-stage disease

claims.text: Non-small cell, resectable: platinum doublet (cisplatin with vinorelbine, docetaxel or paclitaxel; carboplatin if cisplatin can't be used), with or without immunotherapy.
claims.quote: Neoadjuvant therapy in early-stage NSCLC is also commonly used and consists of 4 cycles of a platinum-doublet (usually a combination of a cisplatin and another chemotherapy agent, such as vinorelbine, docetaxel, or paclitaxel) or 3 cycles of a platinum-doublet plus immunotherapy. In patients who cannot receive cisplatin, carboplatin can be substituted.
targeted therapy directed at the actionable mutation should be given as first-line therapy.
Osimertinib is the treatment of choice for EGFR-mutant NSCLC
Patients who have EML4::ALK translocations should receive alectinib or lorlatinib
Patients with BRAF mutations benefit from the BRAF inhibitors (eg, dabrafenib, trametinib).

claims.text: No driver mutation: chemotherapy plus an immune checkpoint inhibitor
claims.quote: In patients with NSCLC without an oncogenic driver mutation, the treatment of choice is chemotherapy plus immunotherapy
Several immune checkpoint inhibitors (nivolumab, ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, durvalumab, cemiplimab, atezolizumab) are available for NSCLC treatment
